summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinvijaya. He held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1945–1965), Gujarat University (1965–1975), and the L.D. Institute of Indology (~1975–2001).

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, and was appointed to the Punjabi and Sikh studies chair at the University of British Columbia (~1987).
Harogadde Manappa Nayak was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1959–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin was an anthropologist and linguist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and Yale University. He held academic posts at Columbia University (1955), Yale University (1962–1996), and the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

Harold Edward Musson worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Wellington College, St Edmund's School, and Magdalene College, Cambridge, and under Buddhist teachers Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Pelene Siri Vajiragnana, after serving in the Royal Artillery and Intelligence Corps.

Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from McMaster University. He served as professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and as director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

Harold Hargreaves worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After serving as headmaster at Government High School, Amritsar (~1904–1908), he held positions including Superintendent and Deputy Director General at the Archaeological Survey of India between 1910 and 1931.

Harold Herman Bender worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lafayette College, Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and Berlin under Richard Pischel and Wilhelm Schulze, later serving as assistant professor at Princeton University (1909–1950).

Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Following teaching posts at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was a humanities professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney (~1937–1939).

Harold Walter Bailey worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Western Australia and the University of Oxford, and held posts at SOAS (1929–1936) and the University of Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University and Oxford, and under Ghulam Yazdani. His career included posts at Osmania University (~1919–1948), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).

Harry Campbell Norman was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Trinity College, Oxford. In 1905, he was appointed Professor of English Literature at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Harry Charles Purvis Bell was an Indologist and historian who studied at Cheltenham College (1864) and joined the Ceylon Civil Service in 1873.

Harry Falk is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ulrich Schneider and Gaya Charan Tripathi. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1978–1993) and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2012).
Harry Halén is a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Pentti Aalto (~1965–1975) and served as an amanuensis at the University of Helsinki (~1970–2008).

Harsha Gautam is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Texas at Austin. She held fellowships and appointments at UT Austin and the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

Harshit Mishra is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Delhi, the International School for Jain Studies, Central Sanskrit University, and Ghent University. In 2024, he served as a Research Associate at the International School for Jain Studies.

Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi. He has held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Weller and Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.
